# epgsql - PostgreSQL driver for Erlang, internal documentation

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/overview-summary.html

This document is made mostly as internal documentation. It can be useful if you plan to contribute some patches to epgsql, want to implement custom datatypes or commands or to better understand epgsql internals.

End-user interface is described in [README.md](https://github.com/epgsql/epgsql#readme).

Epgsql has 3 end-user API interfaces:

All 3 interfaces communicate with [ epgsql_sock](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_sock.html) gen_server, which holds all
the connection state. While

`epgsql_sock` holds all the state, it doesn't know
much about Client-Server communication protocol.
All the communication logic between epgsql and PostgreSQL server is implemented
as a `epgsql_sock` acts as an executor for those commands.`epgsql_wire``epgsql_binary``epgsql_sock` holds an internal state of `epgsql_binary` codecs as well. The
main contents of this state is the mapping between PostgreSQL unique numeric
datatype IDs (OIDs) and callbacks which will be used to decode this datatype.
This mapping is handled by [ epgsql_oid_db](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_oid_db.html) module and is populated at
connection set-up time by

`epgsql_cmd_connect`Most of the connection initialization (network connection, authentication, codecs)
is performed by [ epgsql_cmd_connect](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_connect.html) command, which is just a regular command
(but quite complex one) and can be replaced by own implementation if needed.

Client can execute a number of built-in commands as well as define their own.
See [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html) and all the

`epgsql_cmd_*` pages.
There exists a `epgsql_codec``epgsql_codec_*` pages for more details.
There exists a *Generated by EDoc*

Tells server that the transfer of COPY data is done

Stops copy-mode and returns the number of inserted rows.`copy_from_stdin(C, SQL) -> any()`

Equivalent to [ copy_from_stdin(C, SQL, text)](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#copy_from_stdin-3).

`copy_from_stdin(C:: connection(), SQL::sql_query(), Format::text | {binary, [epgsql_type()]}) -> epgsql_cmd_copy_from_stdin:response()`

`SQL`: have to be `COPY ... FROM STDIN ...` statement

`Format`: data transfer format specification: `text` or `{binary, epgsql_type()}`. Have to
         match `WHERE (FORMAT ???)` from SQL (`text` for `text`/`csv` OR `{binary, ..}` for `binary`).

returns: in case of success, `{ok, [text | binary]}` tuple is returned. List describes the expected
         payload format for each column of input. In current implementation all the atoms in a list
         will be the same and will match the atom in `Format` parameter. It may change in the future
         if PostgreSQL will introduce alternative payload formats.

Switches epgsql into COPY-mode

When `Format` is `text`, Erlang IO-protocol should be used to transfer "raw" COPY data to the
  server (see, eg, `io:put_chars/2` and `file:write/2` etc).

When `Format` is `{binary, Types}`, [ copy_send_rows/3](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#copy_send_rows-3) should be used instead.

`{epgsql, connection(), {error, epgsql:query_error()}}` (similar to asynchronous notification,
  see `set_notice_receiver/2``copy_from_stdin`
  and all the subsequent IO-protocol requests will return error.
  It's important to not call `copy_done` if such error is detected!

`copy_send_rows(C:: connection(), Rows::[tuple() | [bind_param()]], Timeout::timeout()) -> ok | {error, ErrReason}`

`Rows`: might be a list of tuples or list of lists. List of lists is slightly more efficient.

Send a batch of rows to `COPY .. FROM STDIN WITH (FORMAT binary)` in Erlang format

`equery/3``copy_from_stdin/3``Rows` should match the number of elements in `{binary, Types}`).

# Module epgsql_sock

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_sock.html

**See also:** [epgsql_cmd_connect for network connection and authentication setup](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_connect.html).

GenServer holding all the connection state (including socket).

Commands in PostgreSQL protocol are pipelined: you don't have to wait for reply to be able to send next command. Commands are processed (and responses to them are generated) in FIFO order. eg, if you execute 2 SimpleQuery: #1 and #2, first you get all response packets for #1 and then all for #2:> SQuery #1 > SQuery #2 < RowDescription #1 < DataRow #1.1 < ... < DataRow #1.N < CommandComplete #1 < RowDescription #2 < DataRow #2.1 < ... < DataRow #2.N < CommandComplete #2

   `epgsql_sock` is capable of utilizing the pipelining feature - as soon as
   it receives a new command, it sends it to the server immediately and then
   it puts command's callbacks and state into internal queue of all the commands
   which were sent to the server and waiting for response. So it knows in which
   order it should call each pipelined command's `handle_message` callback.
   But it can be easily broken if high-level command is poorly implemented or
   some conflicting low-level commands (such as `parse`, `bind`, `execute`) are
   executed in a wrong order. In this case server and epgsql states become out of
   sync and [ epgsql_cmd_sync](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_sync.html) have to be executed in order to recover.

`epgsql_cmd_copy_from_stdin``epgsql_cmd_start_replication``copy_state() = #copy{initiator = pid(), last_error = undefined |  epgsql:query_error(), format = binary | text, binary_types = [epgsql:epgsql_type()] | undefined}`

`error() = {error, sync_required | closed | sock_closed | sock_error}`

**abstract datatype**: `pg_sock()`

`repl_state() = #repl{last_received_lsn = integer() | undefined, last_flushed_lsn = integer() | undefined, last_applied_lsn = integer() | undefined, feedback_required = boolean() | undefined, cbmodule = module() | undefined, cbstate = any() | undefined, receiver = pid() | undefined, align_lsn = boolean() | undefined}`

`tcp_socket() =  gen_tcp:socket()`

`transport() = {call, any()} | {cast, pid(), reference()} | {incremental, pid(), reference()}`

# Module epgsql_wire

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_wire.html

Interface to encoder/decoder for postgresql
   [wire-protocol](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-message-formats.html)

`include/protocol.hrl`.
`packet_type() = byte()`

see protocol.hrl -type packet_type(Exact) :: Exact. % TODO: uncomment when OTP-18 is dropped

**abstract datatype**: `row_decoder()`

| [build_decoder/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#build_decoder-2) | Build decoder for DataRow. |
| [decode_columns/3](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#decode_columns-3) | decode RowDescription column information. |
| [decode_complete/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#decode_complete-1) | decode CcommandComplete msg. |
| [decode_data/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#decode_data-2) | decode row data. |
| [decode_error/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#decode_error-1) | decode ErrorResponse
  See http://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/interactive/protocol-error-fields.html |
| [decode_message/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#decode_message-1) | tries to extract single postgresql packet from TCP stream. |
| [decode_parameters/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#decode_parameters-2) | decode ParameterDescription. |
| [decode_strings/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#decode_strings-1) | decode multiple null-terminated string. |
| [encode_bind/4](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_bind-4) | encodes `Bind`packet. |
| [encode_close/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_close-2) | encodes `Close`packet. |
| [encode_command/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_command-1) | Encode iodata with size-prefix (used for `StartupMessage`and`SSLRequest`packets). |
| [encode_command/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_command-2) | Encode PG command with type and size prefix. |
| [encode_copy_done/0](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_copy_done-0) | encodes `CopyDone`packet. |
| [encode_copy_header/0](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_copy_header-0) | encode binary copy data file header. |
| [encode_copy_row/3](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_copy_row-3) | encode binary copy data file row / tuple. |
| [encode_copy_trailer/0](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_copy_trailer-0) | encode binary copy data file header. |
| [encode_describe/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_describe-2) | encodes `Describe`packet. |
| [encode_execute/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_execute-2) | encodes `Execute`packet. |
| [encode_flush/0](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_flush-0) | encodes `Flush`packet. |
| [encode_formats/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_formats-1) | encode expected column formats. |
| [encode_parameters/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_parameters-2) | encode parameters for 'Bind'. |
| [encode_parse/3](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_parse-3) | encodes 'Parse' packet. |
| [encode_query/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_query-1) | encodes simple 'Query' packet. |
| [encode_standby_status_update/3](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_standby_status_update-3) | encode replication status message. |
| [encode_sync/0](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_sync-0) | encodes `Sync`packet. |
| [encode_types/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_types-2) | encode types. |
| [format/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#format-2) | Returns 1 if Codec knows how to decode binary format of the type provided and 0 otherwise. |

Build decoder for DataRow

`decode_columns(Count::non_neg_integer(), Bin::binary(), Codec:: epgsql_binary:codec()) -> [epgsql:column()]`

decode RowDescription column information

`decode_complete(Bin) -> any()`

decode CcommandComplete msg

decode row data

decode ErrorResponse
  See `http://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/interactive/protocol-error-fields.html`

tries to extract single postgresql packet from TCP stream

`decode_parameters(X1::binary(), Codec:: epgsql_binary:codec()) -> [epgsql_oid_db:type_info() | {unknown_oid, epgsql_oid_db:oid()}]`

decode ParameterDescription

`decode_strings(Bin::binary()) -> [binary(), ...]`

decode multiple null-terminated string

`encode_bind(PortalName::iodata(), StmtName::iodata(), BinParams::iodata(), BinFormats::iodata()) -> { packet_type(), iodata()}`

`BinParams`: see [ encode_parameters/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#encode_parameters-2).

`encode_formats/1`encodes `Bind` packet.

`encode_close(What::byte() | statement | portal, Name::iodata()) -> { packet_type(), iodata()}`

`What`: see `encode_describe/2`

encodes `Close` packet.

`CloseComplete` response

`encode_command(Data) -> any()`

Encode iodata with size-prefix (used for `StartupMessage` and `SSLRequest` packets)

Encode PG command with type and size prefix

encodes `CopyDone` packet.

`encode_copy_header() -> any()`

encode binary copy data file header

See`encode_copy_row(ValuesTuple, Types, Codec) -> any()`

encode binary copy data file row / tuple

See`encode_copy_trailer() -> any()`

encode binary copy data file header

See`encode_describe(What::byte() | statement | portal, Name::iodata()) -> { packet_type(), iodata()}`

`What`: might be `?PORTAL` (results in `RowDescription` response) or `?PREPARED_STATEMENT`
    (results in `ParameterDescription` followed by `RowDescription` or `NoData` response)

encodes `Describe` packet.

`encode_execute(PortalName::iodata(), MaxRows::non_neg_integer()) -> { packet_type(), iodata()}`

`PortalName`: might be an empty string (anonymous portal) or name of the named portal

`MaxRows`: how many rows server should send (0 means all of them)

encodes `Execute` packet.

`MaxRows` packets of `DataRow` type followed by `CommandComplete` (when no
  more rows are available) or `PortalSuspend` (repeated `Execute` will return more rows)

encodes `Flush` packet.

encode expected column formats

`encode_parameters(Parameters::[{ epgsql:epgsql_type(), epgsql:bind_param()}], Codec::epgsql_binary:codec()) -> iolist()`

encode parameters for 'Bind'

`encode_parse(Name::iodata(), SQL::iodata(), ColumnEncoding::iodata()) -> { packet_type(), iodata()}`

`ColumnEncoding`: see `encode_types/2`

encodes 'Parse' packet.

Results in`ParseComplete` response.

`encode_query(SQL) -> any()`

encodes simple 'Query' packet.

`encode_standby_status_update(ReceivedLSN, FlushedLSN, AppliedLSN) -> any()`

encode replication status message

encodes `Sync` packet.

`ReadyForQuery` response
`encode_types(Types, Codec) -> any()`

encode types

`format(Column, Codec) -> any()`

Returns 1 if Codec knows how to decode binary format of the type provided and 0 otherwise

# Module epgsql_cmd_connect

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_connect.html

**Behaviours:** [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html).

Connects to the server and performs all the necessary handshakes.

Special kind of command - it's exclusive: no other commands can run until this one finishes. It also uses some "private" epgsql_sock's APIs`connect_error() = invalid_authorization_specification | invalid_password | {unsupported_auth_method, kerberosV5 | crypt | scm | gss | sspi | {unknown, integer()} | {sasl, [binary()]}} | {sasl_server_final, any()} |  epgsql:query_error()`

`response() = connected | {error,  connect_error()}`

| [execute/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#execute-2) | |
| [handle_message/4](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#handle_message-4) | |
| [hide_password/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#hide_password-1) | this function wraps plaintext password to a lambda function, so, if
  epgsql_sock process crashes when executing `connect`command, password will
  not appear in a crash log. |
| [init/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#init-1) | |
| [open_socket/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#open_socket-2) | |
| [opts_hide_password/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#opts_hide_password-1) | Replace `password`in Opts map with obfuscated one. |

`execute(PgSock, Connect) -> any()`

`handle_message(X1, Message, Sock, State) -> any()`

`hide_password(Password::iodata()) -> fun(() -> iodata())`

this function wraps plaintext password to a lambda function, so, if
  epgsql_sock process crashes when executing `connect` command, password will
  not appear in a crash log

`init(Opts) -> any()`

`open_socket(SockOpts::[{atom(), any()}], ConnectOpts:: epgsql:connect_opts_map()) -> {ok, gen_tcp | ssl, gen_tcp:socket() | ssl:sslsocket()} | {error, any()}`

`opts_hide_password(Opts) -> any()`

Replace `password` in Opts map with obfuscated one

# Module epgsql_cmd_equery

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_equery.html

**Behaviours:** [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html).

**See also:** [epgsql_cmd_parse](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_parse.html).

Performs 2nd stage of
  [
  extended query protocol.](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-flow.html#PROTOCOL-FLOW-EXT-QUERY)

`statement()` and bind-parameters for placeholders and produces
  query results.
  > Bind < BindComplete > Execute < DataRow* < CommandComplete > Close < CloseComplete > Sync < ReadyForQuery

`response() = {ok, Count::non_neg_integer(), Cols::[ epgsql:column()], Rows::[tuple()]} | {ok, Count::non_neg_integer()} | {ok, Cols::[epgsql:column()], Rows::[tuple()]} | {error, epgsql:query_error()}`

| [execute/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#execute-2) | |
| [handle_message/4](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#handle_message-4) | |
| [init/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#init-1) |

`execute(Sock, Equery) -> any()`

`handle_message(X1, Bin, Sock, Equery) -> any()`

`init(X1) -> any()`

# Module epgsql_cmd_batch

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_batch.html

**Behaviours:** [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html).

Execute multiple extended queries in a single network round-trip

There are 2 kinds of interface:`statement()``statement()````
  > {Bind
  <  BindComplete
  >  Execute
  <  DataRow*
  <  CommandComplete}*
  > Sync
  < ReadyForQuery
```
`arguments() = { epgsql:statement(), [[epgsql:bind_param()]]} | [{epgsql:statement(), [epgsql:bind_param()]}]`

`response() = [{ok, Count::non_neg_integer(), Rows::[tuple()]} | {ok, Count::non_neg_integer()} | {ok, Rows::[tuple()]} | {error,  epgsql:query_error()}]`

`state() = #batch{batch = [[ epgsql:bind_param()]] | [{#statement{name = string(), columns = [#column{name = binary(), type = epgsql:epgsql_type(), oid = non_neg_integer(), size = -1 | pos_integer(), modifier = -1 | pos_integer(), format = integer(), table_oid = non_neg_integer(), table_attr_number = pos_integer()}], types = [epgsql:epgsql_type()], parameter_info = [epgsql_oid_db:oid_entry()]}, [epgsql:bind_param()]}], statement = #statement{name = string(), columns = [#column{name = binary(), type = epgsql:epgsql_type(), oid = non_neg_integer(), size = -1 | pos_integer(), modifier = -1 | pos_integer(), format = integer(), table_oid = non_neg_integer(), table_attr_number = pos_integer()}], types = [epgsql:epgsql_type()], parameter_info = [epgsql_oid_db:oid_entry()]} | undefined, decoder = epgsql_wire:row_decoder() | undefined}`

| [execute/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#execute-2) | |
| [handle_message/4](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#handle_message-4) | |

# Module epgsql_cmd_squery

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_squery.html

**Behaviours:** [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html).

Executes SQL query(es) using
  [
  simple query protocol](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/protocol-flow.html#id-1.10.5.7.4)

> Query < (RowDescription? < DataRow* < CommandComplete)+ < ReadyForQuery --- > Query when len(strip(Query)) == 0 < EmptyQueryResponse < ReadyForQuery

# Module epgsql_cmd_copy_from_stdin

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_copy_from_stdin.html

**Behaviours:** [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html).

Tells server to switch to "COPY-in" mode

See [ https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-copy.html](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/sql-copy.html).
   See

When `Format` is `text`, copy data should then be delivered using Erlang
   [io protocol](https://erlang.org/doc/apps/stdlib/io_protocol.html).
   See [ file:write/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/file.html#write-2),

`io:put_chars/2``\.` at the end of TEXT or CSV data stream is not needed.When `Format` is `{binary, [epgsql_type()]}`, recommended way to deliver data is
   [ epgsql:copy_send_rows/3](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql.html#copy_send_rows-3). IO-protocol can be used as well, as long as you can
   do proper binary encoding of data tuples (header and trailer are sent automatically),
   see

`INSERT` or `SELECT` statement and call `epgsql:parse/2``#statement{columns = [#column{type = TypeName}]}` with correct type names.[ epgsql_cmd_copy_done](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_copy_done.html) should be called in the end.

This command should not be used with command pipelining!

> SQuery COPY ... FROM STDIN ... < CopyInResponse > CopyData* -- implemented in io protocol, not here > CopyDone | CopyFail -- implemented in epgsql_cmd_copy_done < CommandComplete -- implemented in epgsql_cmd_copy_done

`response() = {ok, [text | binary]} | {error,  epgsql:query_error()}`

| [execute/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#execute-2) | |
| [handle_message/4](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#handle_message-4) | |
| [init/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#init-1) |

`execute(Sock, Copy_stdin) -> any()`

`handle_message(X1, Error, Sock, Copy_stdin) -> any()`

`init(X1) -> any()`

# Module epgsql_cmd_start_replication

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_start_replication.html

**Behaviours:** [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html).

Requests server to start sending replication packets

See`epgsql:connect/1``replication` parameter.
  > SimpleQuery "START_REPLICATION ..." < CopyBothResponse | Error

`response() = ok | {error,  epgsql:query_error()}`

| [execute/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#execute-2) | |
| [handle_message/4](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#handle_message-4) | |
| [init/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#init-1) |

`execute(Sock, Start_repl) -> any()`

`handle_message(X1, Data, Sock, State) -> any()`

`init(X1) -> any()`

# Module epgsql_cmd_parse

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_parse.html

**Behaviours:** [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html).

Asks server to parse SQL query and send information aboud bind-parameters and result columns.

Empty`Name` creates a "disposable" anonymous prepared statement.
  Non-empty `Name` creates a named prepared statement (name is not shared between connections),
  which should be explicitly closed when no logner needed (but will be terminated automatically
  when connection is closed).
  Non-empty name can't be rebound to another query; it should be closed for being available again.
  > Parse < ParseComplete > Describe < ParameterDescription < RowDescription | NoData

`response() = {ok, #statement{name = string(), columns = [#column{name = binary(), type =  epgsql:epgsql_type(), oid = non_neg_integer(), size = -1 | pos_integer(), modifier = -1 | pos_integer(), format = integer(), table_oid = non_neg_integer(), table_attr_number = pos_integer()}], types = [epgsql:epgsql_type()], parameter_info = [epgsql_oid_db:oid_entry()]}} | {error, epgsql:query_error()}`

| [execute/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#execute-2) | |
| [handle_message/4](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#handle_message-4) | |
| [init/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#init-1) |

`execute(Sock, Parse) -> any()`

`handle_message(X1, Bin, Sock, State) -> any()`

`init(X1) -> any()`

# Module epgsql_cmd_copy_done

Source: https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_copy_done.html

**Behaviours:** [ epgsql_command](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_command.html).

**See also:** [epgsql_cmd_copy_from_stdin](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm/epgsql_cmd_copy_from_stdin.html).

Tells server that the transfer of COPY data is done.

It makes server to "commit" the data to the table and switch to the normal command-processing mode.`response() = {ok, Count::non_neg_integer()} | {error,  epgsql:query_error()}`

| [execute/2](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#execute-2) | |
| [handle_message/4](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#handle_message-4) | |
| [init/1](https://epgsql.hexdocs.pm#init-1) |

`execute(Sock0, St) -> any()`

`handle_message(X1, Bin, Sock, St) -> any()`

`init(X1) -> any()`
